community.reason: Level 2: all qualifying activity is employee development ($200 million in employee learning programs plus tuition reimbursement), which caps Community at 2, and no external education or community investment is described.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1: the filing gives only a general welcoming statement and workforce demographic statistics, with no specific inclusion practice, network or customer-access program.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: small business lending appears only as one item in a product list, with no named enabling program or reach indicators, so it counts as serving small businesses (lower level chosen when torn between 1 and 2).

notes: The Human Capital section covers only internal workforce topics (compensation, benefits, $200M in employee development, work-life programs). It says nothing about external education, philanthropy, community investment, employee resource groups or customer accessibility, so Community and Cross-cultural are marked insufficient and should get the sustainability-report second look. The Community Reinvestment Act appears only as a regulatory requirement and was not counted as an activity. The $200M figure includes required risk and regulatory compliance training, which on its own would score only 1; it is counted here under employee development. Several trap terms were excluded: 'stockholders' equity', 'diversified set of banking... products', 'investment banking', 'merchant banking' (a regulatory category), 'innovations' and non-U.S. operations. Item 1 incorporates further information by reference from the 2025 Annual Report to Shareholders, which was not provided. The filing also notes an ongoing FRB consent order (the asset cap was removed June 3, 2025) and an OCC AML formal agreement; these are context only.
